SME research | NSE: SSEGL | ISIN INE0RFP01011 | Universe position 356

Information cutoff: **20 October 2026**. Market reference: **19 October 2026**, close **₹375.30**. Research prepared 24 October 2026 from cutoff-eligible disclosures. All monetary amounts are ₹ crore unless explicitly identified as rupees, lakh, shares or tonnes. This is research, not a personal allocation recommendation.

## 1. Executive Verdict

Sathlokhar is a rapidly scaling industrial turnkey EPC contractor, not a software-like compounder or a simple low-P/E bargain. Like-basis Ind AS revenue rose from ₹369.69 crore in FY2025 to ₹820.28 crore in FY2026, and Q1FY2027 continued growing. Named industrial clients, integrated delivery capabilities, repeat orders and an unmodified latest audit are meaningful strengths. The decisive risk is **cash tied up before certification and collection**: FY2026 contract assets were ₹234.47 crore, retention ₹52.86 crore and inventories ₹138.39 crore. Reported CFO was −₹162.95 crore; even removing ₹42.43 crore of FD movements leaves −₹120.52 crore. New PEB capacity may improve execution, but inauguration does not establish commercial output or ownership of related businesses.

At ₹375.30, the current-share TTM P/E is 10.32×. That is not enough to validate investment attractiveness because the October cash, debt, collateral and collections bridge is missing. **BQS NS, GQS NS with a cash-quality cap of 5, IAS NS.** These are incomplete assessments, not zero scores or a finding of insolvency. The useful action is a tightly specified evidence watchlist: verify cash conversion, financing availability and related-party land completion before promoting any conditional valuation into a buy level. No validated compounder designation is warranted. [Latest annual report](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_30589_SSEGL_2025_2026_A_4099325_25082026153058.pdf), [Q1 results](https://www.sathlokhar.com/pdf/Financial_Q1.pdf).

## 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence

The exact issuer is **Sathlokhar Synergys E&C Global Limited**, CIN L45400TN2013PLC092969. Earlier legal names were Sathlokhar Synergys Private Limited and Sathlokhar Synergys E&C Global Private Limited. It listed on NSE Emerge on 6 August 2024. The original listing circular already used **SSEGL**: SATHLOKHAR in archive filenames is not evidence of a former exchange ticker. The FY2026 report discusses additional compliance after capital exceeded ₹25 crore; this is not proof of completed main-board migration. The dated 19 October security master still identifies the SM series and 200-share lot.

Financial scope is **standalone** throughout. No subsidiary, associate or joint venture is disclosed for FY2026. Archivo Infra Inc and Sathlokhar Industries Private Limited are related entities, not subsidiaries whose gross sales can be added to the issuer's revenue. First Ind AS statements are FY2026, with transition on 1 April 2024 and a restated FY2025 comparison. Original AS and IPO-restated AS series are separately retained.

Current issued shares: **25,978,592**; outstanding warrants: **375,000**; potential fully diluted shares: **26,353,592** before hypothetical new financing. The current market capitalization is **₹974.98 crore**. Horizon: five years, with a ten-year sensitivity. Equity hurdle: **15% nominal INR**, with 12%/18% tests. Independent WACC range: 14–18%, reflecting a small, concentrated contractor with financing and execution risk, not inferred from the desired equity return. ## 4. Business Overview

Sathlokhar designs and executes industrial/commercial buildings, warehouses, manufacturing facilities and associated civil, steel/PEB, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, utilities, solar and interior works. Its economic role is to manage a complex delivery chain rather than to sell a proprietary recurring product. Revenue is recognized as construction progresses, often before formal client certification and invoicing. Customer advances and supplier credit can finance part of the cycle, but unbilled work, retention, procurement inventory, tax credits and guarantees consume capital.

The issuer reports a single EPC segment. End-use exposure includes food and beverages, consumer goods, footwear, logistics and industrial production. The latest rating describes approximately 90% revenue concentration in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Geographic concentration can support operational density but exposes the firm to local approvals, labour, weather and regional investment cycles. The report's project-count and manpower claims are management descriptions, not independent proof of market share, capacity utilization or return on capital.

Recognized customer concentration is more important than a decorative logo list. FY2026 anonymous customer A contributed ₹300.9201 crore, about 36.69% of revenue. In FY2025, the three disclosed large-customer amounts totalled ₹190.5545 crore, about 51.55% of restated revenue. The annual report does not reconcile anonymous customer A to a named order award; this research does not infer the identity. Named orders and recognized revenue measure different things.

A project's economics depend on bid discipline, design changes, procurement prices, subcontractor productivity, certification, retention release and final settlement. Fixed or partially fixed pricing can turn an apparently strong order book into poor cash economics if input costs or completion times move against the contractor. EPC collection risk is therefore modeled through operating assets and liabilities, not by applying a generic sales multiple. [Annual report, notes 1, 2 and 44](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_30589_SSEGL_2025_2026_A_4099325_25082026153058.pdf).

## 5. Moat / Industry Position

The plausible advantage is integrated execution: fewer interfaces for the customer, promoter experience, local supplier/subcontractor knowledge, qualifying credentials and repeat industrial relationships. These can help win projects and execute faster. The evidence does not establish an enduring toll-road franchise, captive customer, proprietary technology, network effect or price leadership. PWD/electrical qualifications expand eligibility but competitors can also qualify. Concentration in one large customer and tender-based competition limit bargaining power.

The following are **named primary-source economic comparisons**, not automatic valuation peers. Figures use FY2026 consolidated audited statements for peers versus Sathlokhar standalone. Operating EBITDA excludes other income and financing costs consistently; Techno's discontinued wind profit is not included in its operating EBITDA. No same-date peer market prices/shares were independently assembled, so there is no fabricated peer P/E ranking.

PSP shows how construction cash flow can improve sharply through customer/other liabilities even while receivables rise; its ₹559.86 crore increase in other liabilities is a specific reason not to equate one strong CFO year with permanent cash quality. Techno illustrates that even a larger, established EPC business can experience substantial working-capital absorption, but its power-sector, investment and data-center exposures differ materially. Techno's auditor also emphasizes₹88.528 crore of substantially overdue receivables and other financial assets for which management, relying on its assessment, legal views and interim regulatory orders, recorded no impairment. The opinion is unmodified, but that uncertainty belongs in the peer comparison; it is not a finding about Sathlokhar. Neither comparison excuses Sathlokhar's cash shortfall or proves a premium multiple. They establish a competitive and capital-cycle context. [PSP audited results, PDF 6–9](https://www.pspprojects.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Q4-Result_Signed.pdf), [Techno audited results](https://www.techno.co.in/public/uploads/2/2026-05/audited_2025_26_q4_annual_results.pdf).

The moat would strengthen if repeat customers accepted better pricing/payment terms, concentration fell without margin sacrifice and independently verified collections kept pace with growth. It would weaken if wins required larger unbilled balances, longer retention or related-party sourcing without demonstrable cost benefits.

## 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path

The strongest bear case is not that the issuer has no real projects. It is that recognized revenue and reported profit continue growing while certification and collection lag, inventory accumulates and customer advances fail to keep pace. The linked bear model uses contract assets40% of sales, trade AR14%, inventory19%, retention8%, customer advances4%, EBITDA margin11%, ₹25 crore collection loss and₹30 crore remaining plant capex. Funding must absorb these together, not as disconnected one-variable warnings. It fails even the bounded-finance regime in the dated path table. This is a **modeled shortfall under assumptions**, not evidence the actual company defaulted.

A genuine adverse outcome could require expensive equity issuance, asset sales, reduced work intake, supplier extensions or a restructuring that transfers value away from existing shareholders. A large order book can increase rather than reduce risk when each rupee of execution needs additional unreleased cash. Customer advances reduce working capital but remain obligations to perform; they are not distributable excess equity.

A separate illustrative liquidation stress on the March31 snapshot recovers cash100%, FDs50%, invoiced AR60%, contract assets35%, retention40%, inventory50%, PPE/CWIP/intangibles40% and supplier advances25%, with no recovery assigned to GST/tax/other assets. Gross recovered assets are₹274.50 crore before 10% realization costs, against₹313.82 crore of debt, leases, supplier/operating claims, customer advances, employee claims and the stated tax sensitivity. The modeled equity residual is₹0.00 crore. This is not legal advice on creditor priority or an actual liquidation valuation; the haircuts are analyst assumptions and bank security/offset rights are not resolved. It is kept separate from ordinary going-concern returns and excludes the later June land transaction to avoid mixing dates.

The strongest favorable counterevidence is substantial realized revenue/PAT growth, clean latest financial/IFC opinions, reported absence of debt default, a positive-outlook investment-grade rating, cash-credit access, meaningful equity and repeat industrial orders. Better collections could release substantial capital. That is why the conclusion is pending evidence, not an allegation of fraud or inevitable insolvency.

The thesis-break variable is **net cash released from certified/unbilled work after inventory, retention and security collateral needs**, not revenue growth alone. A verified worsening of contract assets and inventory alongside shrinking available facilities would invalidate a self-funded growth thesis even if EPS still rises. Conversely, two reporting periods of positive FD-adjusted operating cash, normal certification aging and adequate committed headroom would materially strengthen it.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.content_markdown:
Sathlokhar is a rapidly scaling industrial turnkey EPC contractor, not a software-like compounder or a simple low-P/E bargain. Like-basis Ind AS revenue rose from ₹369.69 crore in FY2025 to ₹820.28 crore in FY2026, and Q1FY2027 continued growing. Named industrial clients, integrated delivery capabilities, repeat orders and an unmodified latest audit are meaningful strengths. The decisive risk is **cash tied up before certification and collection**: FY2026 contract assets were ₹234.47 crore, retention ₹52.86 crore and inventories ₹138.39 crore. Reported CFO was −₹162.95 crore; even removing ₹42.43 crore of FD movements leaves −₹120.52 crore. New PEB capacity may improve execution, but inauguration does not establish commercial output or ownership of related businesses.

At ₹375.30, the current-share TTM P/E is 10.32×. That is not enough to validate investment attractiveness because the October cash, debt, collateral and collections bridge is missing. **BQS NS, GQS NS with a cash-quality cap of 5, IAS NS.** These are incomplete assessments, not zero scores or a finding of insolvency. The useful action is a tightly specified evidence watchlist: verify cash conversion, financing availability and related-party land completion before promoting any conditional valuation into a buy level. No validated compounder designation is warranted. [Latest annual report](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_30589_SSEGL_2025_2026_A_4099325_25082026153058.pdf), [Q1 results](https://www.sathlokhar.com/pdf/Financial_Q1.pdf).

The exact issuer is **Sathlokhar Synergys E&C Global Limited**, CIN L45400TN2013PLC092969. Earlier legal names were Sathlokhar Synergys Private Limited and Sathlokhar Synergys E&C Global Private Limited. It listed on NSE Emerge on 6 August 2024. The original listing circular already used **SSEGL**: SATHLOKHAR in archive filenames is not evidence of a former exchange ticker. The FY2026 report discusses additional compliance after capital exceeded ₹25 crore; this is not proof of completed main-board migration. The dated 19 October security master still identifies the SM series and 200-share lot.

Financial scope is **standalone** throughout. No subsidiary, associate or joint venture is disclosed for FY2026. Archivo Infra Inc and Sathlokhar Industries Private Limited are related entities, not subsidiaries whose gross sales can be added to the issuer's revenue. First Ind AS statements are FY2026, with transition on 1 April 2024 and a restated FY2025 comparison. Original AS and IPO-restated AS series are separately retained.

Current issued shares: **25,978,592**; outstanding warrants: **375,000**; potential fully diluted shares: **26,353,592** before hypothetical new financing. The current market capitalization is **₹974.98 crore**. Horizon: five years, with a ten-year sensitivity. Equity hurdle: **15% nominal INR**, with 12%/18% tests. Independent WACC range: 14–18%, reflecting a small, concentrated contractor with financing and execution risk, not inferred from the desired equity return. Liquidity reference is ₹5 lakh, not the user's actual position.

| Gate | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | Conditional | Latest financial/IFC opinions are clean; historical controls and related-party capital allocation need monitoring. No evidenced integrity failure. |
| G2 | Hold / unresolved | Original FY2023/FY2024 audit reports are absent; material accounting-basis/weighted-EPS changes and the 3-/5-year capital bridge remain unresolved. This does not label the latest audited P&L unreliable. |
| G3 | Hold / unresolved | October cash, debt, deposit availability and unbilled collections are not verified. Conditional model shortfalls are not actual defaults. |
| G4 | Conditional | Sixty sessions and current lot are verified. Reference capacity is reasonable, but live depth, spread, restrictions and queues are not verified. |

Aggregate BQS, GQS and IAS confidence is **Low**, because the weakest material missing areas govern the overall conclusions even where individual factors have Medium confidence.

Confidence is High on the latest filed P&L, dated security identity and September ownership; Medium on operating economics and revenue history; Low on current funding availability and mature incremental returns. G2 Hold does not allege unreliable latest accounts. It records missing original audit-report pages, historical reconciliation limitations and an incomplete long-run capital bridge. No failed gate is asserted without evidence. Raw public sources retrieved after cutoff were used only for disclosures dated on or before cutoff; no later reported business outcome is smuggled into the thesis.

| Measure | Known K | Coverage | Raw bound | Cap | Final bound | Point |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BQS | 4.740 | 88.00% | 4.860–5.940 | None | 4.860–5.940 | NS |

| IAS | 1.600 | 30.00% | 2.300–8.600 | None | 2.300–8.600 | NS |

NS is not a neutral score, zero, midpoint or invitation to redistribute weights. For incomplete composites, K is the sum of known weighted contributions; m is the original weight of missing factors; bounds are [K+m, K+10m]. They are mathematical bounds, not confidence intervals. The GQS cap narrows its final bound to 5–5 but **does not cure CAP missingness**, so the point remains NS. No governance-failure or funding-failure override is applied because those failures are not established.

BQS weights: GOV .20, MOAT .20, REV .12, DUR .10, CAP .12, CASH .10, BAL .08, EXEC .08. GQS weights: REV .40, DUR .20, EARN .15, CAP .15, CASH .10. IAS weights: final BQS .25, R .35, D .20, P .10, L .10. Each sums to exactly 1.00. Canonical factors are reused, not re-scored to manipulate separate rankings. BQS known contribution is 4.74 at 88% coverage; GQS known contribution is 5.75 at 85% coverage. IAS known contribution is 1.60 at 30% original-component coverage. Its direct missing-component bound is 2.30–8.60; using the narrower BQS mathematical bound gives a supplementary nested bound of 3.265–7.585, still not a point or probability.

| Factor | Score | Confidence | Rationale |

| GOV | 5 | Medium | Mixed governance evidence, not an integrity failure. Control observations and related-party capital allocation prevent a high score. |
| MOAT | 5 | Medium | Integrated EPC capability and client access are useful but contestable; no demonstrated pricing power or switching-cost moat. |
| REV | 8 | Medium | Five-year AS FY2020–FY2025 revenue CAGR starts in>=30%band9; Medium comparability confidence caps at8. No speculative order/pipeline bonus. |
| DUR | 6 | Medium | Specific industrial capex projects and repeat customers support a runway, but duration depends on order replenishment and collections. |

| EXEC | 6 | Medium | Revenue and signed orders demonstrate delivery, while certification, cash and new capacity remain milestones rather than completed promises. |
| EARN | 7 | Medium | Most current profit is operating and per-share progress is substantial, though cash validation and denominator changes prevent an exceptional rating. |
| R | NS | Low | Unsupported actual entry funding bridge means no defensible base-return factor, despite fully linked conditional diagnostic paths. |
| D | 4 | Medium | Material impairment/recapitalization risk under credible linked collection stress; numerical liquidating stress and cashshortfalls shown separately from ordinary returns. |

### Evidence, counterevidence and confidence for all 13 factors

**GOV evidence.** FY2026 financial and IFC opinions are unmodified; the audit trail reportedly operated throughout the year, was preserved and showed no tampering. Promoter ownership is58.27% with no reported encumbrance; related purchases of₹18.246 crore and the₹15.09 crore related land transaction require arm’s-length scrutiny. Counterevidence: FY2025 bank returns differed and late forms recurred, but latest CARO reports agreement and directors say forms were regularized. No finding establishes fraud. Evidence IDs: S356_AR26, S356_AR2025, S356_SHP_SEP26, S356_MONITOR_JUN26.

**MOAT evidence.** Integrated design, civil, PEB and MEP delivery and repeat industrial orders can reduce customer coordination risk. FY2026 revenue of₹820.28 crore demonstrates larger-project execution; qualifications provide access, not an exclusive franchise. Counterevidence: One customer contributed36.69% of revenue and approximately90% came from three states. Competitive bidding and larger PSP/Techno businesses demonstrate alternatives. Evidence IDs: AR26, CRISIL, orders_oct, PEER1, PEER2.

**REV evidence.** Six original AS observations increase from₹65.0684 crore to₹399.3653 crore; the five-interval pre-pandemic starting point reduces FY2021 trough bias. Latest comparable Ind AS revenue grew from₹369.6852 crore to₹820.2799 crore; Q1FY2027 grew66.82%. Counterevidence: Price/volume mix and certification timing are not separated. AS-to-IndAS restatement reduces FY2025 revenue₹29.6801 crore, so that break is not chained into the CAGR. Evidence IDs: fy2021, fy2022, fy2023, fy2024, ar2025, AR26, q127.

**DUR evidence.** October confirmed business of₹1,239 crore excluding GST supports demand visibility after deducting execution; new named awards have February–August2027 deadlines. Industrial, warehouse, food and footwear end uses provide different demand sources; expanded PEB capacity could support delivery. Counterevidence: The₹1,239 crore includes₹204.81 crore already recognized in Q1 and unknown Q2 execution. The₹23,505 crore bid pipeline is not orders; concentration and short project cycles limit duration. Evidence IDs: orders_oct, call27q1, AR26.

**CAP evidence.** Opening Ind AS contract-asset recognition of₹22.4222 crore changes the capital base; IPO restatement and earlier AS classifications also differ. FY2026 ONWC, FD deployment and the PEB land advance are material; the latest two-year Ind AS diagnostic is calculated but is not a project IRR. Counterevidence: Rapid operating-profit growth and limited owned physical plant could produce good returns if contracts convert to cash. That favorable possibility is not ignored or mapped to zero. Evidence IDs: AR26, S356_RESTATED, M01.

**CASH evidence.** FY2025 plus FY2026 CFO totals−₹259.3453 crore against PAT₹116.4672 crore: the ratio of sums is negative. Removing FD movements of₹42.6828 crore and₹42.4340 crore still leaves adjusted CFO−₹174.2285 crore; contract assets₹234.4731 crore and retention₹52.8603 crore create collection risk. Counterevidence: Statutory CFO includes FD movements, overstating pure operating absorption. FY2024 original CFO was positive₹12.1688 crore, and growth working capital can reverse if customers pay. Evidence IDs: AR26, ar2025, C02.

**BAL evidence.** FY2026 equity₹358.9245 crore exceeds bank debt₹89.7480 crore; CRISIL assigns BBB+/Positive to rated cash-credit facilities of₹180 crore. Demand cash₹3.4576 crore and FDs₹90.0012 crore are separate; significant deposits secure obligations or are earmarked, rather than verified free surplus. Counterevidence: No default is evidenced and latest CARO funding findings are favorable. October drawings/availability are unverified, while June unused proceeds₹20.2652 crore are largely committed. Evidence IDs: AR26, CRISIL, S356_MONITOR_JUN26.

**EXEC evidence.** FY2026 revenue grew121.89% on a comparable basis; Q1FY2027 PAT was₹21.4054 crore. Factory inauguration on30August2026 occurred as announced; commercial production milestones can now be monitored. Counterevidence: Inauguration is not licensed commercial output. The June unbilled-cash question was unanswered numerically, and land-object timing slipped beyond March2026. Evidence IDs: AR26, q127, plant_sep, call27q1, S356_MONITOR_JUN26.

**EARN evidence.** Normalized FY2026 operating EBIT₹113.6364 crore excludes₹3.2760 crore other income and adds back₹0.2410 crore exceptional expense; operating margin is13.85%. Ind AS diluted EPS rose from₹15.58 to₹33.08 and comparable TTM PAT is₹94.5177 crore, showing per-share as well as aggregate progress. Counterevidence: FY2025 AS EPS₹20.73 became₹15.58 after both earnings and weighted shares changed. The preferential issue and375,000 warrants dilute ownership. Evidence IDs: AR26, q127, S356_ALLOT_NOV25.

**R evidence.** No Q1FY2027 balance sheet or CFO is supplied; October cash, debt, collateral and land payments are unverified. Every full cash path retains funding caps, fees, dilution and permanent failure suppression; favorable diagnostic returns are not promoted into supported forecasts. Counterevidence: A conditional conversion case can fund growth and earn positive five-/ten-year returns. NS means uncertainty, not an assertion of negative expected return. Evidence IDs: q127, M01, M02.

**D evidence.** The bear combines contract assets40% of sales, invoiced AR14%, inventory19%, lower11% EBITDA and₹25 crore collection loss; bounded funding fails. Audited demand cash₹3.46 crore is thin relative to the₹11.09 crore land balance and working-capital calls; restricted FDs cannot be used twice. Counterevidence: Positive equity, repeat customers and clean latest audits counter insolvency allegations. Actual failure is not established, and favorable collection cases remain funded. Evidence IDs: M01, AR26, S356_MONITOR_JUN26.

**P evidence.** Current market capitalization and earnings multiples use the verified price and dated current shares. Reverse-growth and entry-price grids rerun funding, dilution and terminal reserves; every failed trial is retained with ordinary returns suppressed. Counterevidence: The TTM P/E could look inexpensive if profits convert to cash. Calling it cheap before validating financing would overstate confidence in uncollected earnings. Evidence IDs: M02, C04.

**L evidence.** All60 validated sessions have positive issuer turnover; median₹15.7730 million gives0.634 theoretical days at5% participation for₹500,000. The dated200-share lot costs₹75,060; seven lots costing₹525,420 fit conservative ten-lot daily capacity at5%. Counterevidence: The last session had only₹3,306,810 turnover and33 trades, allowing only two lots at5%. Aggregate capacity is not an executable quote. Evidence IDs: MARKET60, SECURITY19, S356_SHP_SEP26.

The five-year revenue CAGR starts in the ≥30% band, score 9, but Medium comparability confidence caps REV at 8. The latest growth does not earn a second speculative pipeline bonus. GOV and MOAT are the two borderline scored judgments: ±1 in either shifts the BQS bound by ±0.20; moving both together shifts it by ±0.40, equivalent to ±0.10 of IAS's quality contribution if BQS later becomes scoreable. Missingness and cap status are unchanged. Exact Decimal contributions and unrounded bounds are in scores.json; conventional half-up display is used only at presentation.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.content_markdown:
Sathlokhar designs and executes industrial/commercial buildings, warehouses, manufacturing facilities and associated civil, steel/PEB, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, utilities, solar and interior works. Its economic role is to manage a complex delivery chain rather than to sell a proprietary recurring product. Revenue is recognized as construction progresses, often before formal client certification and invoicing. Customer advances and supplier credit can finance part of the cycle, but unbilled work, retention, procurement inventory, tax credits and guarantees consume capital.

The issuer reports a single EPC segment. End-use exposure includes food and beverages, consumer goods, footwear, logistics and industrial production. The latest rating describes approximately 90% revenue concentration in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Geographic concentration can support operational density but exposes the firm to local approvals, labour, weather and regional investment cycles. The report's project-count and manpower claims are management descriptions, not independent proof of market share, capacity utilization or return on capital.

Recognized customer concentration is more important than a decorative logo list. FY2026 anonymous customer A contributed ₹300.9201 crore, about 36.69% of revenue. In FY2025, the three disclosed large-customer amounts totalled ₹190.5545 crore, about 51.55% of restated revenue. The annual report does not reconcile anonymous customer A to a named order award; this research does not infer the identity. Named orders and recognized revenue measure different things.

A project's economics depend on bid discipline, design changes, procurement prices, subcontractor productivity, certification, retention release and final settlement. Fixed or partially fixed pricing can turn an apparently strong order book into poor cash economics if input costs or completion times move against the contractor. EPC collection risk is therefore modeled through operating assets and liabilities, not by applying a generic sales multiple. [Annual report, notes 1, 2 and 44](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_30589_SSEGL_2025_2026_A_4099325_25082026153058.pdf).

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.content_markdown:
The plausible advantage is integrated execution: fewer interfaces for the customer, promoter experience, local supplier/subcontractor knowledge, qualifying credentials and repeat industrial relationships. These can help win projects and execute faster. The evidence does not establish an enduring toll-road franchise, captive customer, proprietary technology, network effect or price leadership. PWD/electrical qualifications expand eligibility but competitors can also qualify. Concentration in one large customer and tender-based competition limit bargaining power.

The following are **named primary-source economic comparisons**, not automatic valuation peers. Figures use FY2026 consolidated audited statements for peers versus Sathlokhar standalone. Operating EBITDA excludes other income and financing costs consistently; Techno's discontinued wind profit is not included in its operating EBITDA. No same-date peer market prices/shares were independently assembled, so there is no fabricated peer P/E ranking.

| FY26 issuer / perimeter | Revenue | Operating EBITDA margin | PAT | CFO | Cash capex | Economic caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PSP Projects Limited / consolidated IndAS FY26 | 3148.66 | 6.00% | 55.52 | 322.82 | 192.96 | Industrial/building construction is a close economic comparison, but PSP is larger and consolidated with subsidiaries/JV. CFO benefits from₹559.8568 crore growth in other liabilities; this is not automatically recurring cash superiority. |
| Techno Electric & Engineering Company Limited / consolidated IndAS FY26 | 3251.63 | 14.20% | 473.87 | -589.96 | 67.11 | Power T&D EPC and data-center buildout have different markets and a large investment book. Discontinued wind PAT₹25.167 crore is included in total CFO/PAT, not operating EBIT. Auditor emphasis concerns₹88.528 crore substantially overdue receivables/other financial assets, unprovided on management/legal assessments; opinion unmodified. Not an equivalent valuation multiple. |

PSP shows how construction cash flow can improve sharply through customer/other liabilities even while receivables rise; its ₹559.86 crore increase in other liabilities is a specific reason not to equate one strong CFO year with permanent cash quality. Techno illustrates that even a larger, established EPC business can experience substantial working-capital absorption, but its power-sector, investment and data-center exposures differ materially. Techno's auditor also emphasizes₹88.528 crore of substantially overdue receivables and other financial assets for which management, relying on its assessment, legal views and interim regulatory orders, recorded no impairment. The opinion is unmodified, but that uncertainty belongs in the peer comparison; it is not a finding about Sathlokhar. Neither comparison excuses Sathlokhar's cash shortfall or proves a premium multiple. They establish a competitive and capital-cycle context. [PSP audited results, PDF 6–9](https://www.pspprojects.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Q4-Result_Signed.pdf), [Techno audited results](https://www.techno.co.in/public/uploads/2/2026-05/audited_2025_26_q4_annual_results.pdf).

The moat would strengthen if repeat customers accepted better pricing/payment terms, concentration fell without margin sacrifice and independently verified collections kept pace with growth. It would weaken if wins required larger unbilled balances, longer retention or related-party sourcing without demonstrable cost benefits.

Five-year AS revenue CAGR, FY2020–FY2025, is **43.75%**, using six observations and five intervals. Three-year AS CAGR, FY2022–FY2025, is **89.72%**, using four observations. The FY2020 starting point is pre-pandemic and avoids presenting the FY2021 trough as an ordinary base. FY2021 contracted markedly before the recovery. Absolute annual additions are shown rather than replacing them with an average addition.

Latest Ind AS revenue rose ₹450.5947 crore, or about 121.89%, in FY2026. Q1FY2027 revenue of ₹204.8058 crore was about 66.82% above the comparable quarter's ₹122.7715 crore. TTM revenue is **₹902.3142 crore**, calculated as FY2026 + Q1FY2027 − Q1FY2026. TTM PAT is **₹94.5177 crore** on the same basis. No quarterly cash flow is invented and Q1 is not multiplied by four to create a forecast.

The standalone perimeter has no disclosed acquisition or subsidiary addition driving the latest growth. Growth is therefore consistent with execution of more/larger contracts, but the company does not disclose a clean volume/price/pass-through mix or organic-acquisition reconciliation for every historical period. This is a scope inference, not proof that every rupee of growth is real physical volume. Input-price pass-through, project mix, catch-up certification and percentage-of-completion estimates can affect recorded revenue.

FY2025 original AS revenue was ₹399.3653 crore. The FY2026 transition bridge reduces it by ₹20.6811 crore through reclassification and ₹8.9990 crore through Ind AS adjustments to ₹369.6852 crore. Combining original AS FY2025 with Ind AS FY2026 without acknowledging this break overstates or distorts comparisons. Original AS, IPO restatement and first-time Ind AS conversion are separate events, not interchangeable labels. [Original FY2025 report](https://www.sathlokhar.com/pdf/Annual-Report-for-the-FY-2024_25.pdf), [transition note 46](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_30589_SSEGL_2025_2026_A_4099325_25082026153058.pdf).

### Order-book arithmetic and execution perimeter

- At 31 March 2026, management reported unexecuted orders of ₹991.39 crore excluding GST. The FY2026 intake figure of ₹1,111.02 crore contains mixed tax bases; no complete cancellation/execution/variation bridge is supplied. It cannot simply be added to opening orders and reduced by revenue.
- The August call described ₹1,015.18 crore of FY2027 total orders including ₹204.81 crore already executed in Q1. Its stated effective remaining amount was ₹810.37 crore.
- The 1 October disclosure reported ₹1,239 crore excluding GST of FY2027 confirmed business, again including Q1 execution. Subtracting known Q1 execution produces **₹1,034.19 crore before unknown Q2 execution**, an upper bound, not the actual October unexecuted order book.
- The new October awards total ₹117.61 crore **including GST**. Grand Atlantia ₹101.19 crore runs to August 2027; Soken ₹9.34 crore to June 2027; Kemin ₹7.08 crore to February 2027. Not all is FY2027 revenue. Each announcement states no related-party relationship.
- The ₹23,505 crore bidding pipeline is an opportunity set, not contracted revenue, cash, market share or a probability-weighted backlog.

[1 October order disclosure](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SATHLOKHAR_01102026200419_IntimationunderRegulation30.pdf), [August call](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SATHLOKHAR_05082026172149_Investor_Presentation_Letter_to_NSE.pdf).

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.content_markdown:
Management's FY2027 ambition of roughly 70% revenue growth and PAT margin above 10% is labeled guidance, not a base fact. The analyst base first forward-year revenue assumption is ₹1,200 crore, below approximately ₹1,394 crore implied by that guidance, followed by 18% annual growth. The bear starts at ₹1,000 crore and 8% growth; bull ₹1,350 crore and 25% growth. These are scenarios, not precise forecasts of fiscal-year reported sales. All forward annual periods run from the market reference date, and the first 12 months are not silently called FY2027.

At a ₹100 crore average executed project equivalent, ₹1,200 crore annual revenue requires roughly twelve equivalents; year-five base sales require materially more. This is an analyst unit-of-scale illustration, not a disclosed average order size. Maintaining the FY2026 largest-customer share at a larger scale would leave an increasingly large single counterparty exposure. A better scaling path needs additional independently paying customers, adequate site teams and suppliers, certifications that turn into bills, and funded guarantees. The large bid pipeline is insufficient evidence for any of those steps.

The new PEB facility was inaugurated on 30 August 2026. Management described capacity rising from around 300 tonnes/month to 1,200–1,500 tonnes/month, or up to 18,000 tonnes/year. It also discussed commercial production roughly 60 working days later, subject to commissioning, tests and licences. At the information cutoff that commercial ramp was not verified. August's indicated ₹180–200 crore annual gross sales differs from the earlier ₹250–300 crore discussion. Captive fabrication used in an EPC project is not a second sale to be added to external project revenue, and related-party plant activity is not automatically consolidated issuer capacity.

The model therefore gives **no separate PEB revenue bonus**. It includes ₹20 crore remaining plant/equipment capex in base and bull, ₹30 crore in bear, plus the verified ₹11.09 crore remaining land consideration. Those remaining capex amounts are analyst assumptions, not a disclosed approved budget. Title, ownership, approvals, independent valuation and gross-versus-captive output remain prerequisites to a mature project-return assessment. [September facility announcement](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SATHLOKHAR_21092026160126_News_Paper_Publication_NSE.pdf).

Working capital is the dominant reinvestment requirement. Base targets are trade receivables 10%, contract assets 28%, retention 6%, inventory 15%, supplier advances 1.5%, GST credits 3.5% and other operating assets 0.6% of annual sales, offset by payables 16%, customer advances 7.5% and accruals 2.5%. Each is rolled monthly rather than replaced by a cash-conversion shortcut. New security/BG collateral grows when annual sales × 2.5% exceeds the existing unearmarked restricted-deposit pool; bear uses 4%. The precise requirement is not lender-confirmed and is sensitized, not treated as a sanction.

GQS is capped because persistent cash weakness remains after adjusting deposit classifications. CAP stays NS because the latest capital conversion has not matured and 3-/5-year comparable invested-capital bridges are not reliable enough. This avoids rewarding accounting profits as if they already demonstrated attractive reinvestment returns.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.content_markdown:
Promoters and managers have substantial construction experience. The 30 September 2026 NSE shareholding XBRL, filed 12 October, confirms promoters hold **15,137,404 shares, 58.27%**, with no reported pledge, non-disposal undertaking or other encumbrance. The three nonzero promoter holdings are T Sangeethaa 14,111,116 shares, T Harshitaa 545,038 and T S Lokesh Krisna 481,250. G Thiyagu's September holding is zero; carrying his earlier FY2026 holding forward would be wrong. A total 4,830,000 shares remains locked to 14 August 2027 under the original listing terms. Public ownership is not identical to immediately liquid free float.

### Audit and control findings, with proper severity

FY2026 financial statements and internal financial controls have **unmodified opinions**, signed by P P N and Company / D Hitesh on 28 May 2026. Revenue recognition is a key audit matter. The auditor reports that the accounting software audit-trail feature operated throughout the year, with no tampering noted and preservation requirements addressed. FY2025 financial/IFC opinions are also unmodified. These findings are favorable and are not relabeled as a qualification.

FY2025 CARO nevertheless identified differences in bank returns: Q1 book debts ₹26.8368 crore differed because bank reporting was restricted to debts under 90 days; Q2 ₹0.8689 crore concerned unreconciled customer advances; Q3 ₹9.2459 crore retention was inadvertently omitted in returns to Union and Canara. The same underlying exposure in two bank returns is not counted twice. FY2026 CARO reports agreement of quarterly statements with books. This is a historical control issue with favorable subsequent evidence, not proof of fraud or a current unresolved ₹9.25 crore cash loss.

Both years' secretarial reports mention delayed forms. FY2026 directors state these were filed with additional fees and none remained pending at year-end. The recurrence remains relevant to compliance discipline, while the reported resolution must also be stated. FY2021 original auditor Muthukumaran's opinion is unmodified; IFC reporting was not applicable. Its annexure contains stale March 2018 headings inside the FY2021 packet, a document-quality caution. FY2022 original audit and IFC opinions are unmodified. The supplied FY2023/FY2024 original PDFs contain signed statements and notes but omit the independent audit-report pages. Missing pages are **not adverse opinions**. Full year-by-year source locators are in audit_inputs.json.

### Related-party economics and minority treatment

FY2026 purchases were ₹14.0945 crore from Sathlokhar Industries and ₹4.1515 crore from Archivo Infra, together ₹18.2460 crore, about 2.46% of total purchases. Closing combined payables were ₹0.8000 crore. A ₹1 crore rental deposit was outstanding with T S Lokesh Krisna, alongside ₹0.2194 crore rent expense. Management states ordinary-course arm's-length terms; no independent counterparty-level cost benchmarking or aging was found. That is a diligence gap, not automatic abuse.

G Thiyagu and T Sangeethaa received ₹3.8773 crore and ₹3.3056 crore respectively in remuneration including commissions, together ₹7.1829 crore, about 8.73% of FY2026 PAT. The actual amounts and prior-year ₹1.9650/₹1.2298 crore are preferable to repeating an inconsistent percentage increase in the remuneration annexure. Related management salary balances of roughly ₹2.27 crore are included in existing salary payables, not added again as a separate model claim.

The CARE monitoring report identifies a **₹15.09 crore** related-party land agreement dated 18 April 2026 with T S Lokesh Krishna for 2.51 acres in Ariyur, Thiruvannamalai. ₹4 crore was advanced by June; ₹11.09 crore remains due by 23 December 2026 under the agreement. **₹23.42 crore is the revised land-object allocation, not the property's price.** Management described a lease/build-first arrangement and registration after approvals, and said a valuation report could be shared. Final title, valuation, approval and settlement evidence is still needed. The monitor reported no object deviation but delays against the original March 2026 land/GCP timetable; it explicitly does not independently audit all underlying certifications.

### Capital and promises versus delivery

| Dated item | Stated objective / promise | Evidence by cutoff | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| August 2024 IPO | Fresh working-capital and corporate funds | 6,638,000 shares at ₹140; gross ₹92.932 crore; FY25 ₹33 crore WC proceeds still in FD | Funding real, deployment/availability must be distinguished |
| November 2025 preferential | Original proposed ₹114 crore | 1,840,600 shares at ₹482 plus 375,000 partly paid warrants; undersubscribed equity by 149,600 shares; revised potential₹106.79192 crore | Not all headline proceeds received |
| June 2026 monitoring | Land, WC and GCP use | ₹93.23567 crore received; about₹72.97 crore used,₹20.27 crore unused | Earmarked cash is not free surplus |
| May 2026 call | Unbilled work converts in 90–120 days | August question about June unbilled balance deferred rather than answered numerically | Conversion not verified |
| August 2026 plan | Facility inauguration30 August | Ceremony documented | Commercial production and returns still pending |
| December 2026 land deadline | Settle remaining consideration | ₹11.09 crore contractual remainder identified | Future claim, not completed purchase proof |

Bonus shares approved in May 2024 changed units, not economic ownership: 31 new shares for every four held, taking pre-IPO shares to 17,499,992. IPO and preferential fresh shares were economic dilution. Current warrants require a further ₹361.50 each, ₹13.55625 crore total, and can lapse if not exercised within 18 months. The ₹120.50 per warrant already received is not counted again. Authorized capital permits 35,000,000 shares, leaving 8,646,408 unissued shares after reserving warrants. Authorization is not a committed financing source. [September XBRL](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/xbrl/SHP_1736373_12102026062339_WEB.xml).

¹ EPS is as disclosed for that statement basis; NS means not transcribed/verified in this dataset, not zero earnings. Full current-share recalculations are separate. Gross profit is ND because the classification of materials, subcontract/direct expenses and work-in-progress does not establish a consistently comparable gross-profit series. Debt/equity not verified for a historical row remain NS. All rows retain their original scope and basis rather than silently choosing the most flattering revision.

### Restatements: separate transition from true corrections

The IPO restatement changes FY2022/FY2023/FY2024 PAT from approximately ₹0.9975/₹5.3956/₹26.1283 crore to ₹0.8787/₹5.4555/₹26.2143 crore. Annexure 5 identifies gratuity, depreciation, tax and prepaid-expense adjustments. This is distinct from the later Ind AS transition. Original FY2022 CFO of ₹4.3970 crore becomes −₹1.2106 crore in the IPO-restated cash flow, materially affected by advance classifications. Therefore a five-year sum mixing these bases would be misleading.

For FY2025, original AS PAT ₹42.7670 crore is reconciled by +₹0.1102 crore reclassification, −₹9.0699 crore Ind AS adjustment and +₹0.3447 crore actual prior-period-error adjustment to ₹34.1520 crore. Original AS accounting already used AS7 construction accounting; Ind AS is not simply the invention of percentage-of-completion revenue. Opening equity at 1 April 2024 changes from approximately ₹40.5307 crore to ₹63.0210 crore, principally through ₹22.4222 crore contract-asset recognition, with separate lease/discounting/tax adjustments and ₹0.1372 crore actual prior-error correction. The bridge sometimes labels other equity as total equity; share capital is added consistently in this analysis.

Note46 expressly identifies prior depreciation treatment that did not comply with Schedule II, and small related tax corrections. Those are genuine disclosed corrections. The much larger Ind AS revenue/contract-asset transition is not automatically an error or fraud. A narrative reference to ₹8.99 crore contract liability is not invented as an additional balance-sheet claim when the bridge treats it as a change in the contract-asset adjustment. That discrepancy is a question for management. The original weighted-average FY2025 share denominator also changed from 20,633,659 to 21,925,325 in the restated comparison. EPS ₹15.58 reconciles to restated PAT and the latter denominator; its change from ₹20.73 is not an arithmetic error, but the denominator revision needs a clear explanation.

### Earnings to operating cash

FY2026 PBT ₹110.4083 crore plus finance ₹6.2631 crore less other income ₹3.2760 crore plus the exceptional ₹0.2410 crore expense gives **normalized operating EBIT ₹113.6364 crore**. Adding ₹0.9683 crore D&A gives operating EBITDA **₹114.6047 crore**. This definition differs from management EBITDA that includes non-operating income. The ₹0.2410 crore add-back is a diagnostic normalization, not a cash inflow. Normalized operating tax is 26%; normalized owner PAT after all finance costs is approximately ₹79.46 crore. Reported PAT remains ₹82.3152 crore. Deferred-tax credits and deposit income are not silently capitalized into recurring EPC value.

FY2026 pre-working-capital operating cash was ₹114.9636 crore. Inventory consumed ₹87.0189 crore; trade receivables released ₹41.1501 crore; other current assets consumed ₹290.5856 crore; other noncurrent financial assets consumed ₹41.5688 crore; other noncurrent assets ₹8.8977 crore; other current financial assets ₹1.0601 crore. Payables, other current liabilities and other financial liabilities funded ₹71.4788, ₹55.5045 and ₹11.2483 crore. Cash from operations before taxes was −₹134.7858 crore, and the separately labeled income-tax line of ₹28.1656 crore produced reported CFO **−₹162.9514 crore**.

The other-noncurrent-asset movement also includes advance-income-tax and government-deposit changes: the separately labeled tax line is not a complete tax-cash classification by itself. These balances are retained in the statutory bridge rather than counted as freely available cash.

The financial-assets lines include FD increases. Reclassifying ₹42.4340 crore of FY2026 and ₹42.6828 crore of FY2025 FD movements outside operating cash yields the analytical comparison below. The adjustment does not make those deposits unrestricted or generate extra cash. It merely separates collateral/cash-allocation movements from operating conversion. The original statutory figures remain visible.

| Comparable basis | ΣCFO | ΣPAT | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| IPO_restated_AS_FY22_FY24 | 13.9610 | 32.5485 | 0.4289 |
| IndAS_FY25_FY26 | -259.3453 | 116.4672 | -2.2268 |
| IndAS_FD_adjusted | -174.2285 | 116.4672 | -1.4959 |

FY2026 cash capex of ₹1.4538 crore is in investing activity and cannot explain −₹162.95 crore CFO. The cash-flow statement also shows a ₹0.0686 crore ROU addition in investing; conventional lease recognition is normally noncash, so the classification deserves clarification rather than a hidden adjustment. FY2026 net equity cash ₹90.4432 crore and bank debt increase ₹80.6974 crore, less finance and lease payments, largely explain financing cash ₹164.5402 crore. This is **externally financed balance-sheet growth**, not demonstrated self-funded compounding.

### Working capital and capital returns

FY2026 average invoiced trade DSO is about **43.35 days**, using total revenue as a credit-sales proxy. Ending contract assets add **104.33 revenue days**, and ending retention another **23.52 days**. These are not a mechanically additive audited DSO: averages versus ending stocks and different collection stages are deliberately distinguished. A claim of 60–75 days after billing does not eliminate the earlier certification interval. Inventory includes ₹112.9194 crore contract WIP and ₹25.4699 crore raw materials. Average inventory/payables days use purchases as a disclosed proxy and are separately retained in metrics.json; there is no confidently comparable manufacturing cash-conversion cycle.

| IndAS date | ONWC | Operating IC | Financing-side IC | Residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | 50.9751 | 55.4264 | 55.4267 | -0.0003 |
| 2025 | 137.6214 | 148.1136 | 148.1136 | 0.0000 |
| 2026 | 336.0171 | 347.3541 | 347.3540 | 0.0001 |

Operating IC includes ONWC, owned fixed/intangible assets, CWIP, ROU assets and relevant security/operating noncurrent deposits. It excludes demand cash, FDs, deferred tax, advance income tax, government-authority deposits (analytically excluded; the source category includes approval/GST-demand items) and the opening₹0.3018 crore deferred IPO financing cost; financing-side IC includes equity, debt, leases, employee provisions and tax claims, less those excluded assets. Small residuals are disclosed rather than plugged into cash. Customer advances, salary, retention payables and statutory accruals are operating financing, not new equity or bank debt.

FY2026 diagnostic post-tax ROIC on average FY2025/FY2026 IC is **33.94%**, versus the analyst WACC range14–18%. The one-year incremental proxy is **24.24%**: ΔNOPAT **₹48.3025 crore** divided by ΔIC **₹199.2405 crore**. Cash capex less owned D&A plus ΔONWC is ₹199.3743 crore; the remaining ₹-0.1338 crore difference reflects ROU net decline, operating deposits/prepaids and rounding. This is not a project IRR or proof that profits were earned on newly deployed capital. Profit timing, unbilled recognition and rapid capital expansion make it fragile. Three- and five-year comparable incremental ROIC and a commissioned-PEB lagged return are **NS**, not annualized from this one-year result. The model's land and CWIP are not depreciated before commissioning; remaining land consideration is capitalized rather than deducted as an operating expense.

### Cash, debt and claims

At 31 March 2026, demand cash was ₹3.4576 crore; current FDs ₹35.9180 crore and noncurrent FDs ₹54.0832 crore, total ₹90.0012 crore. Management describes long FDs principally as security for guarantees/performance obligations. A complete bank-wise lien/release map is absent. The June unused preferential pool of ₹20.2652 crore is a subset of deposits, not an additional asset. Model releases are only for eligible land, WC or GCP uses. No base valuation credits all FDs as free cash.

Bank debt is ₹89.7480 crore, all current/repayable on demand; lease liabilities ₹0.1907 crore; employee gratuity provisions about₹1.7386 crore. Tax payable is zero on the latest audited balance sheet, but ₹8.4391 crore advance income tax and ₹1.1256 crore government-authority deposits (including approval/GST-demand items) are not immediately available cash. Salary and retention payables remain inside ONWC and are not paid twice. A ₹1.1638 crore historical GST-dispute payment sensitivity is separate from confirmed liabilities; current dispute status and deposit offset require verification. There is no assumption that an unresolved tax item is a fresh current default.

[CRISIL's7May2026 assessment](https://www.crisil.com/mnt/winshare/Ratings/RatingList/RatingDocs/SathlokharSynergysEAndCGlobalLimited_May%2007_%202026_RR_391188.html) assigns BBB+/Positive/A2 to ₹200 crore facilities, split₹180 crore cash credit and₹20 crore BG, and describes adequate liquidity. Its utilization period ends February2026 and its cash-accrual concept is not CFO. It is favorable counterevidence, not proof of October availability. Management's later approximately₹250 crore sanction discussion, partly BG, and the shareholder-approved₹450 crore borrowing ceiling are neither cash nor verified unused headroom.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.content_markdown:
At the dated price/shares, market capitalization is ₹974.98 crore, FY2026 current-basic-share P/E **11.84×**, TTM P/E **10.32×** and EV/normalized operating EBITDA approximately **9.26×**. EV uses March debt/leases and demand cash only, so it is explicitly stale-claim indicative, not a verified October enterprise value. Using reported weighted-average EPS33.08 directly against today's price mixes a historical denominator with current capital. Current-share EPS and full warrant dilution are recalculated in metrics.json.

### Conditional cash model, not reconstructed October accounts

The engine starts on 19 October 2026 with a **synthetic sensitivity opening**: March31 operating balances, debt and demand cash held unchanged, current verified issued shares, June earmarked proceeds/land facts, and the known₹4 crore land advance added to committed capital. This combination is deliberately not represented as an observed balance sheet or a reconstructed April–October cash bridge. There is no invented pre-entry cash flow. The alternative opening-debt₹180 crore and cash₹15 crore tests show sensitivity to this unresolved bridge. For this reason **R and P remain NS even when a conditional path succeeds**.

Each monthly period splits customer receipts and procurement/payroll into early/late events, rolls individual WC assets/liabilities, then funds capex, claims, tax and debt payments. A cash reserve is the greater of₹3 crore or 0.5% of annual sales, growing with operations. Raising that reserve is not an expense, but insufficient cash to satisfy it is a funding shortfall. All such shortfalls, including the terminal forward reserve, latch failure permanently. A failed path may retain diagnostic later balances but **has no ordinary terminal equity value, price or IRR**.

Three financing regimes are tested. No-new-finance gives no fresh bank/equity liquidity and includes a12-month demand-debt nonrenewal stress. Rated-limit permits uncommitted renewal and up to₹90.252 crore incremental borrowing, total debt ceiling₹180 crore. Bounded-finance permits up to₹140.252 crore incremental borrowing, total₹230 crore, plus up to₹80 crore gross equity from 19 January 2027. Both bank regimes are limited by a modeled collateral base of 75% of trade AR plus inventory only, excluding unbilled/retention assets and giving FDs zero credit because they may already secure BG obligations. Those haircuts and availability are assumptions, not lender confirmations. The same FD pool is not simultaneously credited to both bank borrowing capacity and BG coverage; separate release/recovery sensitivities do not establish such dual use. Bank fees1%, interest11% base/13% bear, first-draw-month interest and later principal payments are explicitly charged. Debt is not unlimited negative cash.

New equity uses whole shares at 80% of the trial entry price, minimum₹50, with 3% fees and the35 million authorized-share ceiling after reserving warrants. Each changed entry price reruns financing. Warrants, if exercised in May 2027, bring₹13.55625 crore and 375,000 shares simultaneously; already-paid warrant cash is not added again. Nonexercise is tested. No undocumented new issue or future capital raise is called committed.

Terminal operating value is earned next-year FCFF/(WACC−g), not a terminal multiple detached from cash. FCFF deducts maintenance, incremental fixed capital, ONWC growth, extra BG collateral and growth in operating cash reserve. Land remains nondepreciable. Base terminal growth4%, WACC16%; bear3%/18%; bull5%/14%. Only terminal cash above the forward operating reserve is added, with debt, leases and remaining employee claims deducted once. The forward reserve is prefunded at exit; the terminal bridge adds back the discounted first increment already funded, while ongoing reserve growth remains in terminal FCFF, avoiding a double charge. Restricted/earmarked FDs are not credited as surplus in base. Separate50% FD recovery and 8/10/12× EBITDA cross-checks show sensitivity. No interim dividends are invented; retained cash is counted only once.

### Base five-year annual cash bridge

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
The strongest bear case is not that the issuer has no real projects. It is that recognized revenue and reported profit continue growing while certification and collection lag, inventory accumulates and customer advances fail to keep pace. The linked bear model uses contract assets40% of sales, trade AR14%, inventory19%, retention8%, customer advances4%, EBITDA margin11%, ₹25 crore collection loss and₹30 crore remaining plant capex. Funding must absorb these together, not as disconnected one-variable warnings. It fails even the bounded-finance regime in the dated path table. This is a **modeled shortfall under assumptions**, not evidence the actual company defaulted.

A genuine adverse outcome could require expensive equity issuance, asset sales, reduced work intake, supplier extensions or a restructuring that transfers value away from existing shareholders. A large order book can increase rather than reduce risk when each rupee of execution needs additional unreleased cash. Customer advances reduce working capital but remain obligations to perform; they are not distributable excess equity.

A separate illustrative liquidation stress on the March31 snapshot recovers cash100%, FDs50%, invoiced AR60%, contract assets35%, retention40%, inventory50%, PPE/CWIP/intangibles40% and supplier advances25%, with no recovery assigned to GST/tax/other assets. Gross recovered assets are₹274.50 crore before 10% realization costs, against₹313.82 crore of debt, leases, supplier/operating claims, customer advances, employee claims and the stated tax sensitivity. The modeled equity residual is₹0.00 crore. This is not legal advice on creditor priority or an actual liquidation valuation; the haircuts are analyst assumptions and bank security/offset rights are not resolved. It is kept separate from ordinary going-concern returns and excludes the later June land transaction to avoid mixing dates.

The strongest favorable counterevidence is substantial realized revenue/PAT growth, clean latest financial/IFC opinions, reported absence of debt default, a positive-outlook investment-grade rating, cash-credit access, meaningful equity and repeat industrial orders. Better collections could release substantial capital. That is why the conclusion is pending evidence, not an allegation of fraud or inevitable insolvency.

The thesis-break variable is **net cash released from certified/unbilled work after inventory, retention and security collateral needs**, not revenue growth alone. A verified worsening of contract assets and inventory alongside shrinking available facilities would invalidate a self-funded growth thesis even if EPS still rises. Conversely, two reporting periods of positive FD-adjusted operating cash, normal certification aging and adequate committed headroom would materially strengthen it.

A5× outcome in five years requires 37.97% investor CAGR;10× requires 58.49%. Over ten years the respective rates are17.46% and 25.89%. These are shareholder outcomes, not revenue growth targets: issue dilution, margins, reinvestment and terminal claims must all reconcile. The model tests sales growth grids with unchanged base margin discipline and full financing, rather than assuming a5× share price because sales might rise5×.

At the current price,5×/10× prices are₹1,876.50/₹3,753.00 before transaction costs. With today's26,353,592 potential shares and no further issuance, those imply equity values around five/ten times the current fully diluted price-equivalent; actual hypothetical financing can raise the required equity value further. The exact endpoint sales, shares and funded/failed status for every tested growth rate are in model_summary.json and the full canonical paths. No failed trial is discarded to make the feasible subset look typical.

Operationally, the path needs many more executed project equivalents, more independently paying customers, supervisory capacity, supplier credit, guarantee capacity and timely certification. At the base₹100 crore project-equivalent illustration, year-five/ten revenue requirements can be translated into simultaneous annual delivery equivalents; this remains an assumption, not a reported order-size statistic. New PEB capacity is at most one execution component and its captive sales cannot be counted twice. No evidence supports an unlimited addressable share or unbounded project wins.

**Framework outcome classification: Speculative / unsupported for5× and10× at both five and ten years under the current evidence.** The sampled ten-year5× path is conditionally possible but demanding: it requires sustained20% sales growth, supported margins and finance, and is materially changed by the8× normalization above. No tested five-year5×/10× or ten-year10× base-grid path is validated as a supported forecast.

A successful sampled10-year path is possible mathematics, not a probability estimate or validated compounder thesis. Where a high-growth trial fails before the endpoint, its attractive hypothetical earnings do not generate an ordinary shareholder return. Both operational scale and finance must succeed; missing October balance evidence prevents the current report from declaring either multibagger outcome probable.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.content_markdown:
**Pending evidence: fast-growing industrial EPC with unproven cash conversion at its new scale.** It is not an excluded-by-evidenced-failure record, and its incomplete scores must not be ranked as if they were low numerical points. The raw BQS mathematical range sits below a strong-business designation; GQS is constrained by persistent cash absorption despite rapid revenue growth. A compounder label would require scoreable high business quality, durable capital-efficient growth and demonstrated per-share cash economics, none of which can be established solely from the current P&L.

The conditional action is **watchlist / complete diligence**, not a supported purchase or sale instruction. Required evidence is: current audited/reviewed cash/debt and collateral bridge; unbilled-to-billed-to-collected movement; project-level retention/WIP aging; confirmed availability/renewal conditions; land title/valuation/remaining payment; mature PEB operating economics; and a reconciled long-run operating-capital/EPS history. A lower share price can improve valuation but cannot independently solve a cash-funding gap or missing governance evidence.

At the₹5 lakh reference size, historical exchange capacity appears substantially better than many SME names. The60-session median turnover₹15,773,015 versus mean₹21,683,855.67 yields theoretical5% capacity₹788,650.75/day and 0.634 fractional days. A200-share lot costs₹75,060; six lots use₹450,360, while seven lots exceed the reference at₹525,420. Whole-lot conservative capacity is10 lots/day at 5%,4 lots at 2%,21 lots at 10%; seven-lot exit needs1/2/1 days respectively. In the recent20 sessions,5% capacity permits8 lots/day, but2% only 3 lots, needing3 days. All60 observed sessions have positive turnover; there are no missing issuer sessions or observed zero-turnover sessions. The14 September and 2 October404 archive dates are independently verified exchange holidays, not zero-volume sessions.

On19 October itself turnover was only₹3,306,810 across 33 trades, allowing just two whole lots at 5% participation, not the aggregate ten-lot capacity.
